extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers seeking information about the Microsoft Start news app (users, technology observers)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing Microsoft Start — its features, platforms, history, predecessor relationship to Microsoft News/MSN, and product behaviors (notifications, personalization, integration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content sections / topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The app included sections for top stories, regional events, international events, politics, money, technology, entertainment, opinion, sports, and crime, along with other miscellaneous stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the topical categories Microsoft Start provided to users as its primary content organization; implies a rubric of comprehensive topical coverage for a news aggregator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The app was available for Android and iOS devices only; other users used its web version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies supported platforms (Android, iOS, and web). Useful as a functional requirement for reach and compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization — favorite topics and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: It allows users to set their own favorite topics and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates personalization capabilities — users can configure topics and preferred sources so the feed is tailored to individual interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications / breaking-news alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can receive notifications of breaking news through alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes real-time alerting functionality; an expectation for timeliness and push notification support in a modern news app.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can filter preferred news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables control over which publishers or sources appear in the feed, a criterion for source curation and user control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / adjustable font sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can alter font sizes to make articles easier to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accessibility/readability feature allowing users to change text size; relevant to usability and inclusive design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription model and RSS removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally News included an RSS feed, but that capability was removed; Microsoft currently only allows users to subscribe to specified news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents a change in syndication and subscription behavior — moving away from open RSS to curated/limited subscriptions; implies limitations for users who prefer RSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Windows integration — live tile behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: News uses the live tile feature introduced in the Windows 10 Anniversary Update; if a user clicks the News Start menu tile when a particular story is shown, the user will see a link to that story at the top of the app when it launches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes integration with Windows UI (live tiles) and the expected behavior when interacting with those tiles; relevant to platform-specific UX expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email bulletins — 'Start Daily' delivery practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Microsoft sends unsolicited 'Start Daily' news bulletins to its Outlook mail customers unless they block or unsubscribe from the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes an email distribution practice (solicited vs unsolicited) and the opt-out mechanism; relevant to privacy/communication expectations (article marks citation needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding and product lifecycle / integration into Windows taskbar
rubrics_metrics.description: Microsoft Start was the planned successor to Microsoft News and MSN; with the release of Windows 11 Microsoft directly integrated news into the Windows taskbar (later backported to Windows 10); from November 2024 the Microsoft Start website and app were rebranded back to the MSN brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical/organizational criteria about product naming, successor/predecessor relationships, and integration into the OS — useful for understanding product evolution and platform strategy.
